---
# One-page coverage summary of the compiled MYtraits database, for
# taxonomists and botanists. Render from the project root after building
# the database:
#   uvr run build.R
#   quarto render inst/notes/coverage/summary.qmd
# Input:  export/data/curr/MYtraits.rds
# Output: inst/notes/coverage/summary.md (regenerated, never edit by hand)
# Rows are split by basis_of_record: "preserved_specimen" rows come from
# flora treatments; all other rows (field, captive_cultivated) are
# field-measured.
title: "What MYtraits holds: a coverage summary"
format:
  gfm:
    wrap: none
execute:
  echo: false
knitr:
  opts_knit:
    # Run chunks from the project root, so paths match build.R.
    root.dir: "../../.."
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)

# .Rprofile attaches dplyr before Rscript attaches stats, so stats::filter
# would win.
filter <- dplyr::filter

n_top <- 20

db <- readRDS("export/data/curr/MYtraits.rds")

traits <- db$traits |>
  mutate(
    source = if_else(basis_of_record == "preserved_specimen",
                     "Flora", "Field")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    db$taxa |> select(taxon_name, taxon_rank, family),
    by = "taxon_name"
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(traits$source))

no_family <- "(no family: name not aligned)"
n_unaligned <- n_distinct(traits$taxon_name[is.na(traits$family)])
n_families <- n_distinct(na.omit(traits$family))

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

version <- db$build_info$version %||% "unknown"
sha <- str_sub(db$build_info$git_SHA %||% "unknown", 1, 7)

excluded <- db$excluded_data |>
  count(error, sort = TRUE) |>
  with(paste0(str_to_lower(error), " (", fmt(n), ")")) |>
  paste(collapse = "; ")

# Overview ----------------------------------------------------------------

count_all <- function(df) {
  tibble(
    Datasets = n_distinct(df$dataset_id),
    Taxa = n_distinct(df$taxon_name),
    `Species-rank taxa` = n_distinct(
      df$taxon_name[df$taxon_rank %in% "species"]
    ),
    Families = n_distinct(na.omit(df$family)),
    Traits = n_distinct(df$trait_name),
    Rows = nrow(df)
  )
}

overview <- bind_rows(
  traits |> filter(source == "Flora") |> count_all(),
  traits |> filter(source == "Field") |> count_all(),
  count_all(traits)
) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), fmt)) |>
  mutate(Source = c("Flora", "Field-measured", "All"), .before = 1)

# Overlap -----------------------------------------------------------------

taxa_by_source <- split(traits$taxon_name, traits$source) |> map(unique)
taxa_both <- intersect(taxa_by_source$Flora, taxa_by_source$Field)

pairs_by_source <- split(
  paste(traits$taxon_name, traits$trait_name),
  traits$source
) |>
  map(unique)
pairs_both <- intersect(pairs_by_source$Flora, pairs_by_source$Field)

traits_both <- traits |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa_both) |>
  distinct(source, taxon_name, trait_name) |>
  count(source, taxon_name)

overlap_families <- traits |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa_both) |>
  distinct(family = coalesce(family, no_family), taxon_name) |>
  count(family, name = "Taxa in both", sort = TRUE) |>
  rename(Family = family) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

# Coverage by family ------------------------------------------------------

family_cov <- traits |>
  group_by(Family = coalesce(family, no_family)) |>
  summarise(
    Taxa = n_distinct(taxon_name),
    `Flora taxa` = n_distinct(taxon_name[source == "Flora"]),
    `Field taxa` = n_distinct(taxon_name[source == "Field"]),
    Traits = n_distinct(trait_name),
    `Taxon × trait` = n_distinct(paste(taxon_name, trait_name)),
    Rows = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `Fill (%)` = round(100 * `Taxon × trait` / (Taxa * Traits))
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Taxa), desc(`Taxon × trait`))

# Traits with most taxa ---------------------------------------------------

trait_cov <- traits |>
  group_by(Trait = trait_name) |>
  summarise(
    Taxa = n_distinct(taxon_name),
    `Flora taxa` = n_distinct(taxon_name[source == "Flora"]),
    `Field taxa` = n_distinct(taxon_name[source == "Field"]),
    Families = n_distinct(na.omit(family)),
    Datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Taxa)) |>
  mutate(Trait = paste0("`", Trait, "`"))

top_field <- trait_cov |>
  filter(`Field taxa` > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(`Field taxa`)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  select(Trait, `Field taxa`, `Flora taxa`, Datasets)
```

Generated `r format(Sys.Date())` by `inst/notes/coverage/summary.qmd` from
`export/data/curr/MYtraits.rds` (version `r version`, commit `r sha`). Do
not edit by hand.

MYtraits compiles plant trait data for Malaysia from two kinds of source.
**Flora** data are characters transcribed from family treatments (Flora of
Peninsular Malaysia, Tree Flora of Sabah and Sarawak) and taxon
descriptions, so each value describes a species from herbarium specimens.
**Field-measured** data come from studies that measured plants in plots,
gardens or nurseries. Taxon names are aligned with taxonAlign to the World
Checklist of Vascular Plants (WCVP), restricted to taxa with GBIF records in
Malaysia, Brunei and Singapore; a taxon is one aligned name, which may be a
species, an infraspecific taxon, or a genus or family placeholder
(`Genus sp. [...]`).

## Overview

```{r}
knitr::kable(overview, align = c("l", rep("r", 6)))
```

`r if (n_unaligned > 0) paste(fmt(n_unaligned), "taxa have no family because their names are not aligned, so they are counted under their original name. Family counts and the family table understate coverage until they are.") else "Every taxon has a family."`

A further `r fmt(nrow(db$excluded_data))` values were read from the sources
but excluded during the build and are not counted above: `r excluded`.

## Overlap between flora and field data

- **`r fmt(length(taxa_both))`** taxa have both flora and field-measured
  data (`r round(100 * length(taxa_both) / length(taxa_by_source$Field))`%
  of field-measured taxa,
  `r round(100 * length(taxa_both) / length(taxa_by_source$Flora))`% of
  flora taxa).
- **`r fmt(length(pairs_both))`** taxon × trait combinations have values
  from both sources, so flora and field values can be compared directly.
- For taxa in both, the median taxon has
  `r median(traits_both$n[traits_both$source == "Flora"])` flora traits and
  `r median(traits_both$n[traits_both$source == "Field"])` field-measured
  traits.

Families with the most taxa in both:

```{r}
knitr::kable(overlap_families, align = c("l", "r"))
```

## Coverage by family

The `r n_top` families with the most taxa, of `r fmt(n_families)`. *Taxon ×
trait* counts the combinations with at least one value. *Fill* is that
count as a share of taxa × traits recorded for the family.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  slice_head(family_cov, n = n_top),
  align = c("l", rep("r", 7))
)
```

## Traits with the most taxa

The `r n_top` traits with the most taxa, of `r fmt(nrow(trait_cov))`.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  slice_head(trait_cov, n = n_top),
  align = c("l", rep("r", 5))
)
```

The 10 traits with the most field-measured taxa:

```{r}
knitr::kable(top_field, align = c("l", rep("r", 3)))
```
